title: 38-year-old with slowly progressive asymmetric parkinsonism and mild leg posturing

provenance.citation: Synthetic case drafted 2026-10-17 for Rare Disease Detective; not derived from any individual patient.

chief_complaint: "My right side has been slow and stiff for years, and my right foot cramps when I walk."
history_of_present_illness: Seven years of slowly progressive right-sided slowness and stiffness, mild postural tremor of the right hand, and intermittent right foot cramping with inversion during long walks. No clear diurnal variation reported when asked. Sleep does not obviously help. No REM sleep behavior disorder symptoms, no anosmia, no constipation. Started on levodopa by a previous neurologist 4 years ago with good benefit; dose has remained 100 mg TID since, with no wearing-off and no dyskinesia. Seeking a second opinion because 'I was told it's young-onset Parkinson's but it hasn't progressed like they said it would.'

symptom_timeline.event: Right foot cramping with long walks
Diagnosed young-onset PD; levodopa 100 mg TID started with good response
Stable on same dose; no motor fluctuations or dyskinesia

movement_findings.observation: On medication: mild right-hand bradykinesia on finger tapping without decrement.
Mild right-hand postural tremor, 6–7 Hz, low amplitude.
On medication: normal gait; reports foot inversion only when doses are delayed.

neurological_exam.tone: Mild right upper limb rigidity with activation, on medication
neurological_exam.other: Examined on medication, 2 hours after a dose

prior_trials.response: Marked improvement, sustained, no fluctuations or dyskinesia

family_history: Negative for movement disorders as far as the patient knows. Parents alive and well in their 60s. Not adopted.
prior_workup_and_opinions: Previous neurologist: young-onset Parkinson disease. No DAT imaging was performed. No genetic testing.
